It does lazy load the images, but when i resize the browser, the image is gone and i see the black defined for class bxslider . The observed element has the class lazy-background-loaded . But there is no image visible. i fiddled around with rootMargin and scrollMargin . But the image disappears on resize. Is the IntersectionObserver() suitable for a horizontal background-image slide show? Has anyone ever successfully tried to use IntersectionObserver() in this context? Thanks for your answer. //js(loaded in footer) document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => { const targets = document.querySelectorAll('.lazy-background'); const observer = new IntersectionObserver((entries, obs) => { entries.forEach(entry => { if (!entry.isIntersecting) return; const el = entry.target; const src = el.dataset.bgSrc; if (src) el.style.backgroundImage = `url('${src}')`; el.classList.replace('lazy-background', 'lazy-background-loaded'); obs.unobserve(el); }); }, { root: document.querySelector(".bx-viewport"), rootMargin: "0px", scrollMargin: "0px", threshold: 0, }); targets.forEach(el => observer.observe(el)); }); $(document).ready(function() { $(".bxslider").bxSlider(); }); .lazy-background { background-color: #71797E; /* placeholder colour */ min-height: 250px; /* reserve space — prevent CLS */ background-size: cover; background-position: center; }
